mainTopic: Sources for every kind of interest, and why the תורה wrote separate לאוין for רבית, גזל and אונאה.
overview: The ברייתא finishes finding sources that every kind of interest is forbidden. This covers נשך and רבית, money and food, any item at all, and both borrower and lender. רבינא says food-נשך and money-רבית need no special source, because the פסוק in ויקרא places 'נשך ומרבית' between 'money' and 'food'. The גמרא explains that this leaves the ברייתא's גזירה שוה with a different job: carrying 'נשך כל דבר' over to the lender. Then רבא asks why the תורה wrote separate לאוין for רבית, גזל and אונאה. The גמרא first shows that each has a special feature, so none can be learned from just one other. It then shows that גזל can be learned from רבית and אונאה together through their shared feature. So the written לאו of גזל is used for holding back a worker's wages, as a second לאו on top of 'לא תעשק'. Asked why that extra לאו is not applied to רבית or אונאה instead, the גמרא begins answering from the context of the פסוק, and the answer continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The extra words 'נשך כסף' teach רבית of money
steps.stepSummary: Since 'לא תשיך' already forbids נשך on money, the extra words נשך כסף are applied to רבית on money.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the words 'נשך כסף' are not needed to teach נשך on money, because 'You shall not lend with interest to your brother' already says that, use them to teach רבית on money.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes answering where we learn that רבית on money is forbidden. It does this by using an 'extra' phrase in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לא תשיך לאחיך' already forbid נשך on money, so the words 'נשך כסף' seem to add nothing. Using the rule of אם אינו ענין, a phrase that is not needed for its plain subject gets moved to a related subject. Here that related subject is רבית on money.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If it is not needed for this matter.' This rule moves an extra phrase in a פסוק to teach a different matter.

steps.confusionAlert: נשך and רבית are two names the תורה uses for interest. The ברייתא treats each name as its own איסור, so it looks for a source for each one, for both money and food.

phrases.english: If it is not needed for the matter of neshekh of money,
phrases.notes: 'נשך כסף' comes from דברים 23:20, the same פסוק as 'לא תשיך לאחיך'.

phrases.english: since it was already stated
"You shall not lend with interest to your brother,"
apply it to the matter of ribit of money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְנֶשֶׁךְ כֶּסֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא's derivation, which began before this section, of a source for רבית on money.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra phrase נשך כסף is applied to רבית on money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבית on money is forbidden, learned through אם אינו ענין.

steps.title: What about the lender?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know the איסור also applies to the lender, not just the borrower.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I have this only for the borrower. Where do we learn it for the lender?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new question. The sources so far cover the borrower, so where is the lender included? It is setting up the next derivation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source so far covered only one side of the loan. The ברייתא now wants the full set of rules (money, food, נשך, רבית) to apply to the lender too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I have only…', meaning so far the source covers only this case

phrases.english: I have this only for a borrower;
for a lender, from where?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בְּלֹוֶה, בְּמַלְוֶה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the borrower to a new question about the lender.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the full איסור of interest also applies to the lender.

steps.title: A shared word links lender to borrower
steps.stepSummary: Because the word נשך appears for both borrower and lender, every detail that applies to the borrower also applies to the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: נשך is said about the borrower and נשך is said about the lender. For the borrower you made no difference between money and food, or between נשך and רבית. So too for the lender, make no difference between money and food, or between נשך and רבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a גזירה שוה. The same word, נשך, is used for both sides, so the lender gets all the same rules as the borrower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower's איסור was already shown to cover all four cases: money, food, נשך and רבית. The shared word carries that complete picture over to the lender, so the lender needs no separate source for each case.

keyTerms.meaning: A derivation from the same word appearing in two places
You did not make a difference
'Just as… so too…', the comparison form

phrases.english: Neshekh is stated regarding the borrower
and neshekh is stated regarding the lender.
Just as the neshekh stated about the borrower —
you made no difference in it
between money and food,
between neshekh and ribit,
so too the neshekh stated about the lender —
do not make a difference in it
between money and food,
between neshekh and ribit.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמַר נֶשֶׁךְ בַּלֹּוֶה וְנֶאֱמַר נֶשֶׁךְ בַּמַּלְוֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the lender.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on the word נשך gives the lender every rule that applies to the borrower.

steps.title: What about other kinds of interest?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know that interest in any item, not only money or food, is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we include every kind of thing?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks one more question. Money and food are covered, but what about interest paid in other items? It is setting up a פסוק to answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the sources spoke only of money and food. This question widens the איסור to any item at all.

phrases.english: From where do we include anything at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת כׇּל דָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the איסור beyond money and food.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that interest in any item is forbidden.

steps.title: 'Interest of anything' covers all items
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'נשך כל דבר אשר ישך', which includes every item.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'Interest of anything that is lent with interest.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the words 'כל דבר', 'anything', in the פסוק. With this the ברייתא's derivations are complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כל דבר' are broad. They show the איסור is not limited to money and food but covers any item used as interest.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the ברייתא, interest is forbidden for both borrower and lender. It covers both names (נשך and רבית), both money and food, and in fact any item.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"Interest of anything that is lent with interest."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: נֶשֶׁךְ כׇּל דָּבָר אֲשֶׁר יִשָּׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about other items.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'נשך כל דבר' includes interest in any item.

steps.title: רבינא: no special source is needed
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says that neither נשך on food nor רבית on money needs its own derivation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Neither נשך on food nor רבית on money needs a separate פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא disagrees with how the ברייתא worked. He says it did not need to look for extra sources for these two cases. The next steps explain why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא worked hard to find sources for food-נשך and money-רבית, including the אם אינו ענין in step 1. רבינא says those cases are already written plainly in the main פסוק.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Neither neshekh with food
nor ribit with money needs a verse,

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: לָא נֶשֶׁךְ בְּאוֹכֶל וְלָא רִבִּית בְּכֶסֶף צְרִיכִי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the ברייתא's derivations were necessary.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food-נשך and money-רבית need no special derivation.

steps.title: How the verse would have looked if a source were needed
steps.stepSummary: רבינא grants that if the פסוק had linked נשך only to money and מרבית only to food, the ברייתא would be right.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסוק had said 'Your money you shall not give him with נשך, and your food with מרבית', it would be as you say.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא describes a different wording the פסוק could have used. If it had been written that way, the ברייתא would truly need its derivations. This prepares his main point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that imagined wording, each kind of interest sits right next to only one item. Then food-נשך and money-רבית would really have no plain source.

phrases.english: For if it were written:
"Your money you shall not give him with neshekh
and your food with marbit" —
phrases.notes: This isn't the real פסוק, just a made-up wording. The real one comes in the next step.

phrases.english: it would be as you say.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי כְּתִיב אֶת כַּסְפְּךָ לֹא תִתֵּן לוֹ בְּנֶשֶׁךְ וְאׇכְלְךָ בְּמַרְבִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining רבינא's claim by imagining a different wording.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's claim that no extra derivation is needed
steps.raayaSupportSource: A contrast between the imagined wording and the real wording of the פסוק

steps.title: Read both words with both money and food
steps.stepSummary: Because the real פסוק places 'נשך ומרבית' between money and food, both words apply to both items.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that it is written 'Your money you shall not give him with נשך, and with מרבית you shall not give your food', read it like this: 'Your money you shall not give him for נשך and for מרבית', and 'for נשך and for מרבית you shall not give your food.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא shows the real wording of the פסוק. The two words for interest sit between 'your money' and 'your food', so each word can be read with both items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בנשך ובמרבית' sit in the middle of the פסוק, so they connect both backward to 'כספך' and forward to 'אכלך'. That gives all four cases straight from the פסוק, so the ברייתא's extra derivations are not needed.
steps.whatToRemember: רבינא learns all four cases (money and food, נשך and רבית) directly from ויקרא 25:37, because 'נשך ומרבית' stands between 'money' and 'food'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the placement of words in a פסוק can let them connect to the words before and after them. That can replace a whole chain of derivations.

phrases.english: Now that it is written:
"Your money you shall not give him with neshekh
and with marbit you shall not give your food,"
read it this way:

phrases.aramaic: ״אֶת כַּסְפְּךָ לֹא תִתֵּן לוֹ בְּנֶשֶׁךְ וּבְמַרְבִּית״,
phrases.english: "Your money you shall not give him for neshekh and for marbit,"
"and for neshekh and for marbit you shall not give your food."

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דִּכְתִיב אֶת כַּסְפְּךָ לֹא תִתֵּן לוֹ בְּנֶשֶׁךְ וּבְמַרְבִּית לֹא תִתֵּן אׇכְלֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבינא's proof by contrasting the imagined wording with the real one.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both נשך and מרבית apply to both money and food straight from the פסוק, so no special derivation is needed.

steps.title: But the ברייתא itself used a גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבינא: the תנא of the ברייתא said "נאמר, נאמר", which shows he used a גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא of the ברייתא clearly says "it is stated here, and it is stated there". That is the language of a גזירה שוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבינא's claim from Step 6 that no separate derivation is needed. The ברייתא openly used a גזירה שוה to teach this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "נאמר... נאמר" is the standard wording for a גזירה שוה, which links two פסוקים by a shared word. If the ברייתא needed one, how can רבינא, an אמורא, say it is unnecessary? An אמורא is not supposed to argue with a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of a ברייתא or משנה
"It is stated... it is stated", the formula for a גזירה שוה
Linking two laws through a word the two פסוקים share

phrases.english: But isn't the tanna
saying "it is stated", "it is stated"!
phrases.notes: The word נשך is written about both the borrower and the lender, and the ברייתא uses it to link them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנָּא ״נֶאֱמַר״ ״נֶאֱמַר״ קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's conclusion from Steps 6 and 8 using the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that no derivation is needed for נשך on food or רבית on money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly uses a גזירה שוה for this, so saying it is unnecessary contradicts a תנא.

steps.title: The גזירה שוה would only be needed without the פסוק's wording
steps.stepSummary: רבינא means that without the פסוק's arrangement we would have needed a גזירה שוה, but with it we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבינא means: if the פסוק had not been written this way, I would have said we need a גזירה שוה. Now that the פסוק is written this way, the גזירה שוה is not needed for this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבינא by explaining what he really meant. He is not arguing with the ברייתא. He is only saying that the פסוק already teaches this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזירה שוה would have taught that both words apply to both money and food. But the פסוק already puts "נשך ומרבית" between money and food (Step 8), so it teaches this directly. This leaves the גזירה שוה with no job, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: "This is what he means", a clarification of someone's words

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
Had the verse not been stated,
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק from Step 8 that puts נשך ומרבית between money and food.

phrases.english: I would have said we learn it through a verbal analogy.
Now that the verse is stated,
a verbal analogy is not needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the אמורא's words: the claim is conditional, not a disagreement with the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבינא was arguing with the ברייתא's גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבינא only means the פסוק's arrangement already teaches this point, so the גזירה שוה is not needed for it.

steps.title: So what is the גזירה שוה for?
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק already teaches it, why do we need the ברייתא's גזירה שוה at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need the גזירה שוה?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the גזירה שוה is not needed for food and money, the גמרא asks what it does teach. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה is a teaching from סיני, so it must teach something. Since the earlier job is already covered by the פסוק, the גמרא looks for a new job for it.

keyTerms.meaning: "Why do I need it?", asking what something adds

phrases.english: Rather, why do I need the verbal analogy?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the answer in Step 10, which left the גזירה שוה without a purpose.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the גזירה שוה teaches if it is not needed for applying both terms to money and food

steps.title: The גזירה שוה applies the borrower's לאו to the lender
steps.stepSummary: The גזירה שוה teaches that the לאו of "נשך כל דבר אשר ישך", written about the borrower, also applies to the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches that the לאו of "interest on anything that is lent with interest", which is not written about the lender, also applies to the lender.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the גזירה שוה its real job. It carries the prohibition of "נשך כל דבר" from the borrower over to the lender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק "נשך כל דבר אשר ישך" is written in the borrower's section. Through the shared word נשך, the גזירה שוה connects the two sections, so the lender also gets this extra לאו. This way the גזירה שוה still has a purpose, and רבינא and the ברייתא fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: "Interest on anything that is lent with interest", the borrower's לאו

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's גזירה שוה is not wasted. Its job is to apply the borrower's לאו of "נשך כל דבר" to the lender too.

phrases.english: For "interest on anything that is lent with interest,"
which is not written regarding a lender.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְ״נֶשֶׁךְ כׇּל דָּבָר אֲשֶׁר יִשָּׁךְ״ דְּלָא כְּתִב בְּמַלְוֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גזירה שוה teaches that the lender also violates the לאו of "נשך כל דבר אשר ישך".

steps.title: Why three separate לאוין for רבית, גזל, and אונאה?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks why the תורה needed separate לאוין for רבית, גזל, and אונאה, since all three involve taking someone's money wrongly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Why did the תורה need to write a לאו for רבית, a לאו for גזל, and a לאו for אונאה?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבא asks why the תורה wrote three separate prohibitions when they seem to share one idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three are about getting someone else's money in a forbidden way. So it seems the תורה could have written one and we would learn the other two from it. רבא is asking what each one adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Overcharging or underpaying in a sale

phrases.english: Rava said:
Why do I need that the Merciful One wrote
a prohibition for interest, a prohibition for robbery,
a prohibition for overcharging?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לְמָה לִי דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion after the רבית derivations are settled.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why each of the three money-related לאוין must be written separately

steps.title: רבית alone could not teach the others because it is a חידוש
steps.stepSummary: All three are needed. If only רבית were written, we could not learn the others from it, because רבית is unusual: even the borrower is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are all needed. If the תורה had written only the לאו of רבית, we could not learn the others from it, because רבית is a חידוש. The תורה forbade it even for the borrower.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering רבא by showing why each לאו is needed. It starts with רבית and explains why we could not learn גזל and אונאה from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not learn other laws from a law that has a חידוש, an unusual feature. With רבית, even the borrower, who is the one losing money, does an עבירה. In גזל and אונאה only the taker sins, so we could not learn them from such an unusual case.

keyTerms.meaning: "They are needed", the answer that each item teaches something
A law with an unusual feature, which we do not learn other laws from

steps.confusionAlert: Here the borrower is the one losing money, yet the תורה still forbids him. That is exactly what makes רבית a חידוש compared to גזל and אונאה.

phrases.english: They are necessary,
as, if the Merciful One had written only the prohibition of interest,
we could not learn the others from it, because it is a novelty,
since the Merciful One forbade it even for the borrower.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרִיכִי, דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא לָאו בְּרִבִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering רבא's question from Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The לאו of רבית could not serve as a source for the others because it has a חידוש: even the borrower is forbidden. Steps 15 and 16 give the matching reasons for גזל and אונאה.

steps.title: Robbery alone could not teach the others
steps.stepSummary: If only גזל were written, we would say it is forbidden because it is taken against the owner's will, and we would not forbid אונאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the תורה had written the prohibition only about robbery, I would say robbery is forbidden because it is done against the victim's will. But overcharging, which happens in a sale the buyer agreed to, I would say is not forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its answer from Step 14. It shows that the לאו of גזל could not teach us the other two sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גזל has a special harsh feature: it is taken by force. אונאה happens in a willing sale, so a lighter sin might be allowed. That is why the תורה could not rely on גזל alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Overcharging or underpaying in a sale
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written the prohibition only about robbery,
[I would say it is forbidden] because it is against his will,
but overcharging, I would say is not forbidden.
phrases.notes: The same goes for רבית, since the borrower also agrees to pay it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא לָאו בְּגָזֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer of Step 14, moving from רבית to גזל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: גזל is unusual because it is taken by force, so it cannot teach the other two sins.

steps.title: Overcharging alone could not teach the others
steps.stepSummary: If only אונאה were written, we would say it is forbidden because the victim does not know, so he cannot forgive.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had written the prohibition only about overcharging, I would say it is forbidden because the victim does not know he was cheated, so he never gets a chance to forgive it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer to רבא. It shows that אונאה also has a special feature, so it could not teach the other two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אונאה the victim does not know he lost money, so he cannot give up his claim. In גזל and רבית the victim knows, and he could forgive. So we might have thought those two are allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: Each of the three sins has its own special feature: רבית forbids even the borrower, גזל is against the owner's will, and in אונאה the victim does not know. So no single one could teach the others.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written the prohibition only about overcharging,
[I would say it is forbidden] because he does not know [he was cheated], so he cannot forgive it.
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves the ending unsaid: in גזל and רבית the victim knows, so maybe those would be allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא לָאו בְּאוֹנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three-part answer begun in Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אונאה is unusual because the victim is unaware and cannot forgive, so it cannot teach the others.

steps.title: Maybe one can be learned from the other two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא grants that no single sin teaches another, but suggests learning one sin from two of them together.
steps.simpleTranslation: True, one cannot be learned from one. But let one be learned from the other two together! Which one should we learn this way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that all three לאוין are needed. It sets up the next steps, where it will test which sin could be learned from the other two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two sources are joined, the special feature of one is canceled out by the other. So the special features from Steps 14-16 might no longer block the learning. If this works, one לאו would be extra.

phrases.english: One cannot be learned from one.
Let one be learned from two.
Which one should be learned?

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא מֵחֲדָא לָא אָתְיָא. תֵּיתֵי חֲדָא מִתַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer of Steps 14-16 but challenges it with a two-source learning.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that all three לאוין are necessary.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if no single sin teaches another, two together might teach the third, making one לאו extra.

steps.title: Suggestion: learn interest from robbery and overcharging
steps.stepSummary: First try: the תורה could have skipped the לאו of רבית and we would learn it from גזל and אונאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the תורה not write the prohibition about interest, and we will learn it from these two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first specific attempt: learn רבית from גזל and אונאה together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This would make the לאו of רבית extra. The next step tests whether גזל and אונאה share a feature that רבית lacks.

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One not write the prohibition about interest,
and let it be learned from these.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא לָאו בְּרִבִּית, וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers 'which one?' from Step 17 with a specific proposal.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a separate לאו of רבית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: גזל and אונאה together could teach רבית, so its own לאו seems extra.

steps.title: Rejected: robbery and overcharging happen without consent
steps.stepSummary: גזל and אונאה both happen without the victim agreeing, but in רבית the borrower agrees, so they cannot teach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about these two? They happen without the victim's consent. Can you say the same about interest, which the borrower pays willingly?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the attempt to learn רבית from גזל and אונאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both 'teachers' share one feature: the victim did not agree. רבית lacks this feature, since the borrower agreed to pay it. So the לאו of רבית is still needed.

phrases.english: What about these?
They are special because they happen without consent.
Will you say the same about interest, which is with his consent?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהָנָךְ שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the proposal of Step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the attempt to learn רבית from the other two.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: גזל and אונאה share a feature, lack of consent, that רבית does not have.

steps.title: Suggestion: learn overcharging from robbery and interest
steps.stepSummary: Second try: the תורה could have skipped the לאו of אונאה and we would learn it from גזל and רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the תורה not write the prohibition about overcharging, and we will learn it from these two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again, this time learning אונאה from גזל and רבית together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this works, the לאו of אונאה would be extra. The next step checks whether גזל and רבית share something that אונאה lacks.

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One not write the prohibition about overcharging,
and let it be learned from these.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא לָאו בְּאוֹנָאָה, וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first attempt failed, the גמרא tries a different combination.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a separate לאו of אונאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: גזל and רבית together could teach אונאה, so its own לאו seems extra.

steps.title: Rejected: robbery and interest are not normal buying and selling
steps.stepSummary: גזל and רבית do not happen through normal buying and selling, but אונאה does, so they cannot teach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about these two? They are not the normal way of buying and selling. But overcharging happens in ordinary business, so maybe it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the attempt to learn אונאה from גזל and רבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both 'teachers' are outside normal trade: one is robbery, the other is a loan. אונאה happens inside ordinary buying and selling, where people expect to bargain. So it still needs its own לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not the normal way

phrases.english: What about these?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן אֵין דֶּרֶךְ מִקָּח וּמִמְכָּר בְּכָךְ.
phrases.english: They are special because buying and selling is not done this way.
phrases.notes: Left unsaid: would you say the same about אונאה, which does happen in normal business?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהָנָךְ, שֶׁכֵּן אֵין דֶּרֶךְ מִקָּח וּמִמְכָּר בְּכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the proposal of Step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the attempt to learn אונאה from the other two.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: גזל and רבית share a feature, being outside normal trade, that אונאה does not have.

steps.title: Third try: skip the prohibition of robbery
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the תורה could have left out the לאו of גזל and we would learn it from רבית and אונאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, let the תורה not write the prohibition of robbery, and we would learn it from these two (interest and overcharging).
steps.whatsHappening: After two failed tries, the גמרא tries again. This time it suggests dropping the לאו of גזל and learning it from רבית and אונאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method is the same as before: two sins together teach a third. The question now is whether רבית and אונאה share something that also applies to גזל, with no special feature that would block the lesson. The next steps test this.

keyTerms.meaning: Robbery, taking someone's property by force or against their will
A negative commandment in the תורה
And let it be learned from these (other cases)

phrases.english: Rather, let the Merciful One not write
the prohibition about robbery,
and let it be learned from these (two),

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָא לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא לָאו בְּגָזֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third attempt in the same pattern, after steps 18 and 20 were rejected
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a separate לאו of גזל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבית and אונאה together can teach גזל, the written לאו of גזל seems extra

steps.title: Answering the objection that interest is unusual
steps.stepSummary: If someone says רבית is a חידוש and cannot teach, אונאה shows that the lesson still works without that feature.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what objection could you raise? If you say: interest is special because it is a novelty, overcharging proves otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its new suggestion. It knocks down a possible objection against using רבית as a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might say רבית is a חידוש, an unusual rule, so it cannot teach anything else. But אונאה has no such unusual feature and is still forbidden. So the lesson does not depend on רבית being unusual.

keyTerms.meaning: You refute, you raise an objection
A novelty, a rule we would not expect from logic
Will prove, shows that the objection fails

steps.confusionAlert: This step rejects a possible objection, not the suggestion itself. The גמרא is defending the idea that גזל could be learned.

phrases.english: For what objection would you raise?
What about interest? It is a novelty!
Overcharging will prove (that this doesn't matter)!
phrases.notes: אונאה is forbidden even though it isn't a חידוש, so being a חידוש isn't the real reason.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּמַאי פָּרְכַתְּ: מָה לְרִבִּית שֶׁכֵּן חִידּוּשׁ? אוֹנָאָה תּוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends step 22 against a first possible refutation
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects a possible refutation of the derivation
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חידוש feature of רבית is not needed, since אונאה shows the same rule without it

steps.title: Answering the objection that the overcharged victim cannot forgive
steps.stepSummary: If someone says אונאה is special because the victim does not know and cannot forgive, רבית proves that this feature doesn't matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say: overcharging is special because the victim doesn't know about it and so can't forgive it, interest proves otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down a second possible objection, this time against using אונאה as a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אונאה the buyer does not know he was overcharged, so he cannot forgive it. That might make it more serious than גזל. But in רבית the borrower knows and agrees, and it is still forbidden, so not knowing is not the key factor.

phrases.english: What about overcharging?
There the victim doesn't know, so he can't forgive!
Interest will prove (that this doesn't matter)!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְאוֹנָאָה שֶׁכֵּן לָא יָדַע וּמָחֵיל? רִבִּית תּוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends step 22 against a second possible refutation, the mirror image of step 23
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects a possible refutation of the derivation
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The victim's not knowing is not needed, since רבית is forbidden even though the borrower knows

steps.title: The common feature teaches robbery
steps.stepSummary: Since each source covers the other's weakness, the shared feature of רבית and אונאה, taking someone's money, teaches גזל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reasoning goes back to the start. This case is not like that one, and that one is not like this one. What they have in common is that one robs the other. So I will also bring in robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the הצד השוה argument. Without any special feature to block it, רבית and אונאה together teach גזל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source has its own special feature, but the other source shows that the feature doesn't matter. What remains is the part both share: one person wrongly takes another's money. גזל has that same feature, so it should be forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: And the reasoning goes back to its starting point
The feature of this case is not like the feature of that case
The common side, the feature two cases share

steps.whatToRemember: With a הצד השוה, each source's special feature is cancelled out by the other source. Only what they share is used to teach the new case.

phrases.english: And the reasoning goes back to the start:
the feature of this one is not like the feature of that one,
and the feature of that one is not like the feature of this one.
The common side between them
is that he robs him.
So I will also bring in robbery!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין: לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation that steps 23 and 24 defended
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: גזל can be learned from רבית and אונאה through their shared feature of taking another's money

steps.title: Agreed, so why is the robbery prohibition written?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that גזל could be learned, and asks what the written לאו of גזל is for.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Indeed so. But then, why do I need the prohibition written about robbery?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the third try. This raises a new question: what is the written לאו of גזל for? This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא now agrees that regular robbery could be learned from רבית and אונאה. A תורה verse is not written for nothing, so the written לאו of גזל must teach something else.

phrases.english: They said: Indeed so.
But then, why do I need the prohibition about robbery?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הָכִי נָמֵי. אֶלָּא, לָאו בְּגָזֵל לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 25 and asks what the now-extra verse is for
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the written לאו of גזל teaches, if regular robbery is already learned from רבית and אונאה

steps.title: The robbery verse forbids withholding a worker's wages
steps.stepSummary: The written לאו of גזל teaches the prohibition of כובש שכר שכיר, holding back a hired worker's pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is for one who holds back the wages of a hired worker.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the לאו of גזל is used for a new case: an employer who holds back a worker's pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holding back wages does not take anything from the worker. The employer just doesn't pay what he owes. Since that is not the same as taking money, it could not be learned from רבית and אונאה, so the verse is needed to forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: The wages of a hired worker

steps.whatToRemember: Regular robbery can be learned from רבית and אונאה, so the written לאו of גזל is used for holding back a worker's wages. The next step challenges this, and Step 29 refines it into a second לאו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the written לאו of גזל from being wasted. Ordinary robbery is learned through the הצד השוה, so the verse is given a different job.

phrases.english: For one who holds back the wages of a hired worker.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְכוֹבֵשׁ שְׂכַר שָׂכִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The לאו of גזל is used for כובש שכר שכיר, a case that could not be learned from רבית and אונאה

steps.title: Holding back a worker's pay already has its own verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 27: כובש שכר שכיר is already forbidden by an explicit פסוק, so why would we need the לאו of גזל for it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Holding back a hired worker's pay? It is already clearly written about it: 'Do not oppress a hired worker who is poor and needy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 27. It points out that holding back a worker's pay already has its own clear פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 said the written לאו of גזל is needed to teach כובש שכר שכיר. But if the תורה already says 'לא תעשק שכיר' outright, the לאו of גזל would teach nothing new. So the question 'what is the לאו of גזל for?' seems to come back.

keyTerms.meaning: Holding back a hired worker's pay
Clearly, openly, in so many words
Do not oppress (or cheat someone of what is owed to him)

phrases.english: One who holds back a hired worker's pay:
it is clearly written about it:
"Do not oppress a hired worker who is poor and needy"!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהֶדְיָא כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the לאו of גזל is needed to teach כובש שכר שכיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A prohibition that is already written outright does not need a second פסוק to teach it, so the לאו of גזל would be extra.

steps.title: The extra verse adds a second prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The לאו of גזל is not needed to create the prohibition. It is there so that someone who holds back a worker's pay breaks two לאוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is there so that he violates two prohibitions for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The לאו of גזל adds a second prohibition on top of the one already written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא agrees that 'לא תעשק' already forbids holding back pay. The לאו of גזל still has a job: it makes the act count as breaking two לאוין instead of one. So the written לאו of גזל is not wasted.

phrases.english: So that he violates two prohibitions for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לַעֲבוֹר עָלָיו בִּשְׁנֵי לָאוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra פסוק a new job: adding a second לאו
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since כובש שכר שכיר is already written, the לאו of גזל would add nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The לאו of גזל adds a second prohibition, so holding back pay breaks two לאוין.

steps.title: Why not use the extra prohibition for interest or overcharging?
steps.stepSummary: If the לאו of גזל only adds a second prohibition, why apply it to כובש שכר שכיר? It could just as well add a second לאו to רבית or אונאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us apply it to רבית and אונאה, so that a person violates two prohibitions for them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 29. If the job is only to add a second לאו, why should that extra לאו go to holding back pay and not to רבית or אונאה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבית and אונאה also have their own written לאוין, just like holding back pay. So the answer 'it adds a second לאו' fits them equally well. The גמרא wants a reason for choosing כובש שכר שכיר over the other two.

keyTerms.meaning: But let us apply it (to a different case)

phrases.english: But let us apply it to interest and to overcharging,
phrases.notes: "It" is the written לאו of גזל.

phrases.english: so that he violates two prohibitions for them?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלוֹקְמַהּ בְּרִבִּית וְאוֹנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 29
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying the extra לאו of גזל specifically to כובש שכר שכיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Adding a second לאו works just as well for רבית or אונאה, so nothing forces us to apply it to holding back pay.

steps.title: Learning from the surrounding verses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: we read a פסוק based on its context, and that is why the לאו of גזל is applied to holding back pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a matter learned from its context.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer why the extra לאו goes to holding back pay. Its answer is that a פסוק is understood by what surrounds it, and the sentence continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'דבר הלמד מענינו' means a פסוק is read in light of what is written around it. That is the reason the גמרא gives for applying the לאו of גזל to כובש שכר שכיר and not to רבית or אונאה. The details of how the context shows this come right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter learned from its context, meaning the surrounding פסוקים

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the end of the answer. The sentence continues on the next עמוד, where the גמרא shows what the context is.

phrases.english: It is a matter learned from its context,

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד מֵעִנְיָינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of Step 30
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק through its context
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra לאו of גזל could just as easily be applied to רבית or אונאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The context of the פסוק decides where the extra לאו belongs, and it points to כובש שכר שכיר.
